name: Renton
deadline_pattern: Late October to early November each year for the following calendar year (2026 cycle was due 2025-10-24, 4:30 p.m.)
contact: Jessie Kotarski, Economic Development Manager, jkotarski@rentonwa.gov, 425-430-7271
notes: Nonprofits and municipal bodies only (IRS letter, Renton business license and $1M/$2M insurance naming the City required); reimbursement-based, project completed in the same calendar year, 25% match scored.

presentation.pattern: LTAC evaluates applications after the early-November deadline and sends recommendations to Council; no applicant presentation step is described

funding_docs.title: City of Renton Lodging Tax Grant Guidelines
funding_docs.summary: Eligible uses are tourism marketing, event marketing and operations, and nonprofit tourism facility operations; applicants need an IRS determination letter, a Renton business license and $1M/$2M liability insurance naming the City, and awards are reimbursement-based with a 25% match used in scoring.

funding_docs.title: 2026 LTAC Funding Allocation (presentation to Committee of the Whole, Nov 2025)
funding_docs.summary: 20 applications asked for $1,446,444 and LTAC recommended $900,000 to 7 projects, led by $600,000 for the City's Legacy Square Activation, $100,000 for the City marketing campaign and $75,000 for the Chamber's Visitors Center; 13 applicants got $0.

funding_docs.title: 2025 LTAC Funding Allocation
funding_docs.summary: Prior-year allocation table of 2025 lodging tax awards by organization; amounts not extracted.

funding_docs.title: Full list of previously awarded organizations of LTAC funding
funding_docs.summary: Historical list of every organization that received Renton lodging tax funding; amounts not extracted.

pool_note: 2026: fund revenue not published; LTAC recommended $900,000 total, of which $700,000 went to the City's own Legacy Square activation and marketing campaign, leaving $200,000 awarded across 5 outside projects (Chamber $105,000, Niu Wave $55,000, two others $20,000 each).

name: Lynnwood
notes: No outside-organization grant application found; the 2025-2026 budget shows the Lodging Tax Fund ($1.73M for the biennium) funding the city's own tourism program 100%, advised by a Tourism Advisory Committee rather than a grant LTAC.

funding_docs.title: City of Lynnwood 2025-2026 Biennial Budget, Lodging Tax Fund 101
funding_docs.summary: Lodging tax revenue of $1,730,800 for the biennium funds the city's tourism program 100% ($1,902,404 in expenditures, of which $1,734,390 is services and charges and about $168K is staff); no grant program line is shown.

pool_note: 2025-2026 budget: $1,730,800 biennial lodging tax revenue (about $865,400 per year) funds the city's own tourism program 100%, with no outside grant pool.

name: Federal Way
deadline_pattern: Two rounds per year: February 10 (Council approval early May) and August 11 (Council approval early November), 5:00 p.m.
contact: Julianna La Brake, Economic Development, EconomicDevelopment@federalwaywa.gov, (253) 835-2408
notes: Tourism Enhancement Grant runs twice a year (cycle field set to annual) for events and non-event tourism programs; reimbursement-based, with interviews before the LTAC; the official page lists dates without years.

members.name: Stacia Winters
members.affiliation: Federal Way Performing Arts & Events Center (Position 4)

presentation.pattern: Applicants submit a presentation about two weeks after the deadline (Feb 24 / Aug 25) and are interviewed by the LTAC about four weeks after the deadline (Mar 10 / Sep 8, 2:00 p.m.); LTAC decides about five weeks later (Apr 14 / Oct 13)

meeting_schedule: Regular meetings at City Hall, Hylebos Conference Room, 2:00-4:00 p.m. (next listed 2026-12-08); recurrence not published

funding_docs.title: Tourism Enhancement Grant Application (JotForm)
funding_docs.summary: Online application for the twice-yearly Tourism Enhancement Grant funded from the City's 1% lodging tax; reimbursement-based, for events and non-event tourism programs.

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax Advisory Committee Overview, Instructions and TEG Key Meeting Dates
funding_docs.summary: Laserfiche folder holding the LTAC overview, application instructions and the TEG schedule (Feb 10 and Aug 11 deadlines, interviews, LTAC decision, FEDRAC and Council approval); amounts not stated.

funding_docs.title: LTAC meeting packets and agendas
funding_docs.summary: Current and past LTAC agendas and packets, where TEG award recommendations and funding tables are recorded; could not be opened in this session.

funding_docs.title: City approves $39,050 in tourism enhancement grants (Federal Way Mirror)
funding_docs.summary: Example of a spring round: 11 events shared $39,050, the largest being $9,000 (Northwest Global Fest) and $8,850 (Apple Festival Run); indicates typical awards of $700 to $9,000.

pool_note: No current fund total or award list found; the only published award round (spring 2013) split $39,050 across 11 outside events, so the per-round pool is small.

name: Kent
deadline_pattern: Historically September 1-30 for the following calendar year (2018 cycle for 2019 funding)
contact: Michelle Wilmot, Economic Development Manager, mwilmot@KentWA.gov, 253-856-5709 (2018 listing, verify)
notes: Business and leisure tourism promotion grants; applicants were nonprofits, CVBs, PFDs, DMOs, chambers and municipalities; no current-cycle page could be reached, so dates and contact need confirmation.

funding_docs.title: Kent City Council awards $500,600 in lodging tax grants (Kent Reporter)
funding_docs.summary: 33 groups requested about $1.4M; $500,600 of a $546,000 budget went to 23 groups, led by Visit Kent marketing ($96,500), City business marketing ($75,000), Seattle Thunderbirds ($63,555) and accesso ShoWare Center ($60,000).

funding_docs.title: City of Kent to award $200,000 in lodging tax grants (Kent Reporter)
funding_docs.summary: Seven grants totaling $200,000, the largest $60,000 to the Seattle Thunderbirds and others from $9,000 to $50,000; funded that year with federal relief dollars.

funding_docs.title: City of Kent seeks applicants for tourism grants (Kent Reporter)
funding_docs.summary: Applications accepted online September 1-30 for the following year; eligible applicants are nonprofits, CVBs, PFDs, DMOs, chambers and municipalities, and funds must go to marketing and promotion of business or leisure tourism.

pool_note: 2019 estimate: $546,000 lodging tax budget; $500,600 awarded, of which $96,500 went to the Visit Kent DMO contract and $75,000 to City business marketing, leaving about $329,100 for roughly 20 outside events and organizations (a City website item of unknown size is still inside that figure).

name: Bothell
notes: No open grant program found; about $425K/yr in lodging tax mostly funds a Street Sense destination marketing contract (6-month extension approved September 2026), and the LTAC has discussed funding targeted events for 2027-2028.

funding_docs.title: Bothell LTAC meeting summary, April 14, 2026 (Govly)
funding_docs.summary: 2026 lodging tax expenditures budgeted at about $500,000 against a $41,712 beginning fund balance; a two-year $430,000 Street Sense marketing contract is the main commitment, with no grant awards listed.

funding_docs.title: Bothell LTAC meeting summary, March 17, 2026 (Govly)
funding_docs.summary: 2025 revenue was projected at about $425,000 against $470,000 in expenses; the Street Sense contract is about half the budget and the committee discussed shifting toward targeted events for 2027-2028.

funding_docs.title: Bothell LTAC meeting summary, September 15, 2026 (Govly)
funding_docs.summary: Committee approved a six-month, roughly $133,000 extension of the Street Sense marketing contract (two-year value about $412,000).

pool_note: 2026: about $500,000 budgeted lodging tax spending (2025 revenue about $425,000), committed to the Street Sense marketing contract, visitor center support and holiday lighting, with no outside grant pool.

name: Issaquah
deadline_pattern: Two rounds for the May-April funding year: early February (2026 round due 2026-02-06, fixed tiers of $7,500/$10,000/$15,000) and a mid-July second round (due 2026-07-12, up to $55,000)
notes: Issaquah businesses and nonprofits only; first round offers $7,500/$10,000/$15,000 tiers, second round up to $55,000; reimbursement-only, must coordinate with Issaquah hotels and draw visitors from 50+ miles.

presentation.pattern: No presentation at application; LTAC reviews in late July about two weeks after the deadline, but grant recipients must present to the LTAC at a later meeting

funding_docs.title: LTAC 2026-7 Funding Initiative: Second Funding Opportunity (application and criteria)
funding_docs.summary: Issaquah businesses and nonprofits may request up to $55,000 for projects run August 2026 to April 2027; reimbursement only, must coordinate with Issaquah hotels and draw visitors from 50+ miles, and recipients must present to the LTAC.

funding_docs.title: LTAC accepting applications for tourism funding (first 2026 round, posted Jan 6, 2026)
funding_docs.summary: First 2026 round, due February 6, 2026, offered fixed request tiers of $7,500, $10,000 or $15,000 for projects run May 2026 to April 2027; reimbursement only.

funding_docs.title: Tourism Grant Funding Opportunity news release (June 12, 2026)
funding_docs.summary: Announces the second round due July 12, 2026 with requests up to $55,000, reimbursement-based.

pool_note: No fund total or award list found for 2026; the February round offered fixed $7,500/$10,000/$15,000 awards and the July round allowed requests up to $55,000, so the pool is likely low six figures (estimate).

name: Spokane Valley
deadline_pattern: Late October each year (4:00 p.m.) for the following calendar year
contact: Sarah Farr, Accounting and Finance Program Manager, sfarr@SpokaneValleyWA.gov, 509-720-5041
notes: For-profit and nonprofit applicants are eligible; the 1.3% capital portion is limited to municipalities and PFDs; the online application cannot be saved, so prepare the eight required PDFs first.

presentation.pattern: Every applicant gives a 10-minute oral presentation at the LTAC meeting about three weeks after the late-October deadline; slides or video must be submitted with the application

meeting_schedule: Not published; LTAC meets after the grant deadline (2026-11-18 for the 2027 cycle)

funding_docs.title: 2027 Lodging Tax Request for Proposals
funding_docs.summary: Up to $250,000 available, no cap per award, open to local jurisdictions, for-profits and nonprofits for event and tourism-facility marketing and operations; projects are ranked by LTAC within category, reimbursement-based with no match requirement, and every applicant must give a 10-minute oral presentation on November 18, 2026.

funding_docs.title: 2027 Council Goals and Priorities for Lodging Tax
funding_docs.summary: Council guidance LTAC uses to rank proposals, emphasizing events and facilities that build a sports and outdoor recreation identity per the Tourism Strategic Plan.

funding_docs.title: 2025 Lodging Tax Grant Recipients
funding_docs.summary: $393,000 from the 2% tax went to 11 recipients, led by Spokane Valley HUB ($147,000) and JAKT Foundation's Crave! ($50,000); up to $2.5M from the 1.3% capital portion went to the City and Spokane Sports for the Cross Country Course.

funding_docs.title: 2027 Impact on Tourism Template
funding_docs.summary: Required attachment for estimating overnight stays and visitor counts that LTAC uses in scoring.

pool_note: 2025 award list: $393,000 from the 2% tax went to 11 outside recipients (HUB $147,000, Crave! $50,000), with a separate $2.5M from the 1.3% capital portion to the City and Spokane Sports; the 2027 competitive pool is capped at $250,000.

meeting_schedule: Once or twice each fall, dates posted on the public meetings portal

funding_docs.title: Kennewick LTAC and City Council agendas (public meetings portal)
funding_docs.summary: The October 22, 2026 LTAC agenda and the November 18, 2026 Council agenda carry the 2027 lodging tax funding table; amounts were not retrievable in this session.

funding_docs.title: Richland Lodging Tax Grant Program page
funding_docs.summary: Reimbursement-based grants covering up to 30% of a project's total cash expenses for tourism promotion and tourism-related facilities; page could not be opened in this session.

funding_docs.title: City of Richland release: 2026 Lodging Tax Grant Program applications (Oct 3, 2025)
funding_docs.summary: Applications due October 10, 2025 at 5:00 p.m.; grants reimburse up to 30% of total cash expenses; no pool total given.

funding_docs.title: City of Richland release: 2027 Funding Opportunities Open House (June 10, 2026)
funding_docs.summary: Lodging Tax Grant Program listed among 2027 programs with applications opening between July and October 2026; contact Economic Development at (509) 942-7725.

contact: Laurel McQuade, Communications Program Lead, mcquadeL@pasco-wa.gov, 509-975-9683; Richa Sigdel, Deputy City Manager
notes: 2027 window closed and LTAC reviewed in September; prior expenditure plans posted show past awards.

meeting_schedule: Not published; 2027-cycle meeting 2026-09-17, 1:30 p.m., Pasco City Hall, with virtual option on request

funding_docs.title: 2026 Final Lodging Tax Expenditure Plan
funding_docs.summary: $985,223 allocated against $850,000 estimated revenue (gap from fund balance): committed items take $739,723 (GESA Stadium debt $290,000, Tri-Cities VCB $235,220, HAPO Center $200,000), with $46,500 spread over 8 events ($1,000 to $12,500 each), $64,000 for marketing and $135,000 for facility projects.

funding_docs.title: 2027 Lodging Tax Online Application
funding_docs.summary: No request cap, match or point scoring; HAPO Center, Gesa Stadium and tourism promotion contracts have priority, and applicants state full and minimum funding levels, overnight-stay estimates and prior-year success; due July 31 by email to mcquadeL@pasco-wa.gov.

funding_docs.title: 2025 Final Lodging Tax Expenditure Plan
funding_docs.summary: Prior-year allocation table of Pasco lodging tax expenditures by recipient; amounts not extracted.

funding_docs.title: LTAC meeting packets (CivicWeb)
funding_docs.summary: Agendas and packets including the September 17, 2026 meeting where 2027 requests were reviewed.

pool_note: 2026: $850,000 estimated revenue; $739,723 pre-committed to Gesa Stadium debt, the Tri-Cities VCB and HAPO Center, plus City-run events, marketing and $135,000 of facility projects, leaving $29,000 awarded to 6 outside events and Franklin County history ($39,000 more went to the Pasco Chamber for marketing).
